newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatar to open official bourse in Q1 97 - official.
newsitem.headline: Qatar to open official bourse in Q1 97 - official.

text.p: Qatar will open an official stock exchange in the first quarter of 1997, a senior Qatari official said on Saturday.

"The bourse will be known as the Doha Securities Market (DSM) because it will deal with all kinds of shares, bonds and financial instruments issued by the government and its members," said Hussein Abdullah, recently appointed chairman of the DSM.
"It will start functioning in the first quarter of next year," he told reporters.
Abdullah said DSM was currently working on a regulatory framework for the exchange and measures to ensure it attracts a large number of investors.

"A consultant is to be named within this month to help us formulate rules and regulations to protect investors' interests, decide on a trading mechanism and accounting system and select the right technology to facilitate transactions," he said.
Abdullah said the consultant would also help decide whether the bourse should use electronic or floor-based trading and would work on guidelines for listing companies on the exchange.
He said a committee, set up to steer the DSM, was examining reducing the nominal value of shares to be traded on the exchange to boost the volume of transactions.
At present the nominal value of all shares traded on Qatar's unofficial exchange is 100 riyals.
Abdullah said the bourse would not be initially open to expatriates, foreign investors or nationals of other Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) states.
The economic, political and military bloc groups Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, the United Arab Emirates, Oman and Bahrain.
"But in the future, GCC citizens and foreign nationals may be gradually allowed," he said.
"It will also take time to link the Qatari bourse with other bourses in the region" as envisaged by a GCC resolution.
Abdullah said the stock exchange would be autonomous, but indirectly overseen by the ministry of finance, economy and commerce.
Shares in 18 companies are traded on Qatar's current unofficial stock market, which has a total market capitalisation of $1.8 billion.
